mbm-2526.clue: The smallest bar gets the last word.
mbm-2526.quote: My neighbour and I learn marimba tunes from opposite ends of the instrument. When we meet in the middle, the last high bar waits. My little cousin gets to ring it with one mallet.

mbm-2527.clue: I have a shelf for invisible friends.
mbm-2527.quote: I carve a small wooden house every time a new ham operator tells me about their town. A lighthouse, a barn and a blue apartment block crowd my shelf. I know the voices behind every door.

mbm-2528.clue: My ski socks travel in a cake tin.
mbm-2528.quote: My aunt packed them in an empty round tin to keep them dry. At the lodge I lifted the lid and everyone came looking for biscuits. Now I put a biscuit on top of the socks.

mbm-2529.clue: We invented the crooked tree rule.
mbm-2529.quote: Our favorite tree grew round the corner of a fence. Throw a disc through that bent arch and everyone has to applaud, even if it lands in the flower bed. I've applauded the flowers three times.

mbm-2530.clue: I had to learn how to wave with my chin.
mbm-2530.quote: My nephew was so pleased to see me on water skis that he waved his hat with both hands. I kept both of mine on the handle and gave him my grandest nod. At dinner he greeted every dish the same way, even the peas.

mbm-2531.clue: I tucked thunder inside the border.
mbm-2531.quote: During the long storm my aunt and I sewed our quilt by lantern light. We used one jagged silver stitch each time it thundered. It runs along the edge like a little weather chart.

mbm-2532.clue: I followed our tortoise around with a spool of yellow thread.
mbm-2532.quote: I laid yellow thread along the path our tortoise took from the tap to the lettuce patch. I sewed the route into a quilt for my brother. He recognized the long stop under his chair by the enormous knot.

mbm-2533.clue: The coin likes a warm seat.
mbm-2533.quote: I slip a coin under one of three felt coasters. Before I lift the cup, Gran warms her hands over all three like they're tiny stoves. She will not let a conjurer serve cold tea.

mbm-2534.clue: I gave the stage moon a handle.
mbm-2534.quote: I cut a silver moon for our play and fixed a wooden spoon to the back. During the curtain call the smallest actor gets to carry the moon above everybody's head.

mbm-2535.clue: My best pajamas have an opening theme.
mbm-2535.quote: My brother stitched little music notes along their cuffs. When our show starts I wave both sleeves like a conductor. Dad waits till my downbeat before he opens the popcorn.

mbm-2536.clue: My rarest card is a pencil drawing.
mbm-2536.quote: I kept an empty sleeve for years. My little cousin drew me a tired old sea dragon with spectacles and filled it. Nobody at the card table has made me a serious offer because nobody dares.

mbm-2537.clue: The ghost walks in sensible shoes.
mbm-2537.quote: I played a ghost in a white curtain. My squeaky shoes got a bigger laugh than the lines. For our last performance I made the ghost stop and polish one shoe. That brought the house down.

mbm-2538.clue: My quilt team has a sturdy pair of outfielders.
mbm-2538.quote: At our picnic everyone picked an animal for the quilt. My nephew wanted just two rows of red stitches on a round white patch. When I asked which animal it was, he pointed at our two brown bears. He'd made them a ball to play with after bedtime.

mbm-2539.clue: I keep one eye on the ceiling fan.
mbm-2539.quote: I taught myself to juggle with three folded socks. One got stuck on the ceiling fan, and my flatmate turned the switch until I could reach it. That's still my most elaborate catch.

mbm-2540.clue: The armchair has an intermission bell.
mbm-2540.quote: At pajama mysteries we put a bicycle bell beside the oldest armchair. Anyone who guesses the culprit can ring it. The last episode had so much ringing the neighbors asked if we had a new bike.

mbm-2541.clue: I send the weather in two colors.
mbm-2541.quote: I write a ham contact in blue pencil if it's raining here and red if it's raining there. One distant storm traveled clear across my logbook, switching colors as it went.

mbm-2542.clue: My bowling bag has two left feet.
mbm-2542.quote: I embroidered my shoes on the side of my bag before I realized I'd drawn two left shoes. My teammates call them double luck. I leave them facing the pins.

mbm-2543.clue: The smallest scarf is longer than its owner.
mbm-2543.quote: I crocheted a scarf for my niece's toy mouse. The loops got away from me and now it wraps four times round. On cold days his three toy cousins stand inside it too.

mbm-2544.clue: I can draw a whistle from memory.
mbm-2544.quote: I sketch trains with the sound turned into a line above them. A distant whistle is a long loop. The station cat sneezing once made a very short bump beside a huge locomotive.

mbm-2545.clue: I asked the projectionist to keep me one empty reel.
mbm-2545.quote: My favorite cinema closed for a month to mend the ceiling. The projectionist lent me an empty reel for our backyard show. We laid it on the grass, put jam jars through its five holes and lit the path with little lamps. He found his way to the best chair.

mbm-2546.clue: My broom has one row of blue wool.
mbm-2546.quote: I wrapped my curling broom in the yarn left over from my first team scarf. On the white ice it looks like a piece of sky. My skipper calls for the blue broom when a stone starts to curl.

mbm-2547.clue: We vote with buttons after dessert.
mbm-2547.quote: Every new game rule in our house needs three buttons in a saucer before it becomes official. My grandpa spends most of game night guarding his last button against bad ideas.

mbm-2548.clue: I still carry the practice seam.
mbm-2548.quote: My first leather pouch split after a week. I cut out the crooked row of stitching and made it a key fob. It reminds my hands how much straighter they can sew today.

mbm-2549.clue: My postcard rack is all corners.
mbm-2549.quote: I take a picture from one corner of every market I visit. Stack the prints and the awnings make one long roof. I keep the afternoon crowds in a little box under my bed.

mbm-2550.clue: I can hear winter in my towel.
mbm-2550.quote: The wooden shelf at our favorite spring creaks when we lift our towels. After the quiet soak that little creak sounds like a welcome-home song. My sister always gets hers down last to hear it twice.
